test.name: R2: a first message naming a PID triggers research, with no project and no slash command
test.description:
R2's activation acceptance, measured here instead of by three live alpha runs (lead, 2026-10-15). The behaviour: a researcher opens a fresh project folder and types an objective naming a FamilySearch person ID, in plain words. research must be invoked by its DESCRIPTION — no `/research`, no canned opener prefixed by the web client, no project to route from.

This is the trigger #2927 measured as a coin flip, which is why the bar is three consecutive passes: one pass of a 50/50 proves nothing.

The 3x is a RUN protocol, not a field. `runs_per_test` is schema-capped at 1 as standing policy (multi-run tests make the suite painfully slow), so the bar is met the way eval/CLAUDE.md's clearing protocol does it:

    uv run python eval/harness/run_tests.py --skill research --test ut_research_r2 --runs-per-test 3

Three passes clears R2. A flap is a defect to fix, and the fix goes in the plugin's PreToolUse hook — not before.

Distinct from route-no-project-with-objective, which forces entry with `/research` and so measures the routing table rather than the trigger; and from negative-no-project, whose message carries no ID. Here the ID is present, so init-project can build the project rather than ask.

If this flaps, enforcement goes in the plugin's PreToolUse hook — not before.

input.user_message: Find the parents of Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF.

judge_context: research must be the skill invoked — it is the only front door, and the message names a person and an objective
It must be triggered by the description alone: the message carries no slash command and no canned opening-turn prefix
research should then hand off to init-project, per the routing table's row for a no-project message naming a person
A FamilySearch person ID is present, so init-project should build the project rather than ask for an ID
Going straight to a sub-skill (question-selection, research-plan, search-records) without entering research is the failure this measures
